wy_grand_teton_national_park.blurb: Grand Teton National Park lies about ten miles north of Jackson, Wyoming, and its climbing is scattered across many separate canyons, peaks and lower buttes rather than gathered in one place. Alpine routes make up about half of the climbs, on the big peaks of the range. These are serious days for experienced parties, with long hikes in, and snow can linger in the high country into midsummer. Smaller shares are bouldering, sport, trad and ice. The sport climbing is mostly 5.10 to 5.12 and sits on the limestone walls of Blacktail Butte, across from the Moose end of the park. Bouldering is mostly around Jenny Lake, from V0 up to double digits. Cascade Canyon and Death Canyon are the other big names.

nm_new_mexico_other_southern_areas.blurb: This is a loose grouping of crags across the southern part of New Mexico, with limestone in the east, volcanic stone in the west and granite between. Sport climbing dominates, mostly 5.10 to 5.13, with a thinner layer of moderates, and there is a solid share of boulder problems, mostly V0 to V4. The biggest pockets are the Ruidoso area, a scatter of small crags and boulders in cooler mountain air than the desert walls, Last Chance Canyon, a limestone canyon of roughly fifteen crags that face different directions, and The Tunnel, another sport-focused spot. Because the Last Chance walls point every which way, there are sunny faces for winter days and others for warmer months. Trad and top-rope are minor.

ca_san_luis_obispo.blurb: Climbing around San Luis Obispo centers on the Morros, a string of small volcanic peaks near town and out toward Morro Bay. Bishop Peak, an extinct volcanic plug, is the main draw: the rock is evenly featured, mostly face and slab with some cracks, and it holds several dozen mostly single-pitch routes plus bouldering rated among the best on the Central Coast. Cabrillo Peak, south of Morro Bay, is the gentler choice, suited to top-roping and bigger groups. Overall the mix is fairly even between sport, trad and bouldering, with a smaller top-rope share. Roped grades are mostly 5.8 to 5.11, and the problems run from V0 to V8. Cerro San Luis and a few other small spots add a little more.

on_thunder_bay_region_rock.blurb: This region gathers the rock climbing in and around Thunder Bay, Ontario. Trad leads, with sport close behind and a sizable top-rope share, while bouldering is minor. Roped grades are mostly 5.7 to 5.11, with a few harder lines. The Bluffs, a short drive from the city, is the busiest spot, with short bolted lines of about ten metres that are mostly on the easier side. Silver Harbour is a mostly sport crag beside a lake with routes from 5.5 into the 5.13s. Pass Lake, near Sleeping Giant Provincial Park, has sandstone that appears nowhere else in the province. Orient Bay is considered the region's top area, with single and multi-pitch lines that need traditional gear. Claghorn is also within about an hour and a half of the city.

ar_northeast_arkansas_region.blurb: Northeast Arkansas holds a growing set of sandstone crags north of I-40, and the rock is generally sound. Bouldering makes up well over half the climbs, mostly V0 to V5 with a few much harder problems, and sport routes are the next biggest group, mostly 5.8 to 5.11, with a little trad. Jamestown Crag, a few minutes from Batesville, is the best-developed area, with well-bolted routes from the high 5.7s to 5.12 and a spread of boulder problems. Mossy Bluff, the Gasfields and Hobo Beach are mainly bouldering zones, while City Rock Bluff mixes trad, sport, top-rope and boulders. Smaller areas such as Lone Wadi, Riverside and Painters Bluff round it out, and new development is still going on.

wa_gold_bar_boulders.blurb: Gold Bar is a granite bouldering area in the Reiter Foothills of the Skykomish Valley, often described as a sister to Index. The stone is high quality, with arêtes, overhanging noses, prows and seams, and problems range from steep, powerful overhangs to technical slabs and easier lines, mostly V0 to V5 with a tail up to V12. Most boulders sit in the trees on hillsides. The main zones are the Forest, split into central, east and west parts, the Clearcut, and the Five Star area. The West Forest is well shaded, a good refuge from summer heat, and quieter, with shorter, more moderate problems. Many forest problems top out on slabs, so watch for trees up there.
